chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

Concerning a man who performed the obligatory Tawaf and forgot the two Rakʿahs until he had gone between al-Safā and al-Marwah, then remembered, he said: "He marks that place, then returns and prays the two Rakʿahs, then returns to his place."
That was also narrated by Muḥammad ibn Muslim from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

"Whichever of the two reports he follows is valid." He said: And I said to him, 'A man forgot the two Rakʿahs behind Maqām Ibrāhīm عليه السلام and did not remember until he departed from Makkah.' He said: 'Then let him pray them wherever he remembers; and if he remembers them while he is still in the town, then he must not leave until he makes them up.'

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of prayer performed for Tawaf
key_terms.الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: the two points between which Saʿy is performed
key_terms.الْمَكَانَ: the place in Saʿy that should be marked before returning
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory Tawaf that requires the prescribed two Rakʿahs afterward
key_terms.مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: the station of Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, behind which the prayer of Tawaf is performed
key_terms.يَقْضِيَهُمَا: to make up the missed two Rakʿahs

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets the two Rakʿahs of Tawaf and remembers after Saʿy or after leaving Makkah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who forgets the two Rakʿahs of Tawaf during hajj or ʿumrah rites. It explains that he should return to perform them when he remembers, and if he has already left Makkah, he may pray them wherever he recalls them.
